Shares of Avanti Feeds (1,492.60 (7.26 %)) and Apex Frozen Foods (479 . 70 (11.64%)) surged in today’s trading session after strong export data from India’s seafood sector boosted investor confidence. The trigger was a strong export performance that signaled both resilience and future earnings potential – two things investors pay close attention to.

India’s marine exports grew approximately 14% year-on-year in FY26, reaching around $8.43 billion. This growth came as a surprise to the market, beating expectations despite a challenging global environment.

What made this growth particularly significant was the global tariff backdrop. The industry managed to expand despite steep US tariffs, reportedly around ~50% and geopolitical instability in West Asia. Normally, such factors would weigh heavily on export-driven sectors. Instead, the data suggested something more powerful:

This combination tends to boost investor confidence quickly.

A major contributor to this performance is shrimp, which continues to dominate India’s seafood exports by value. Companies like Avanti Feeds and Apex Frozen Foods are deeply tied to shrimp production and exports, making them direct beneficiaries of any surge in demand.

Demand from key international markets has also held steady. The United States alone accounts for about 36% of India’s seafood exports, with China, the European Union, and Japan also playing significant roles. The fact that exports remained strong despite tariff pressures reassured investors that demand hasn’t collapsed. Instead, it reinforced the idea that Indian seafood companies remain relevant and competitive on the global stage.

Momentum and Existing Stock Trends

Stock-specific momentum added fuel to the rally. Apex Frozen Foods has already delivered triple-digit returns over the past year, while Avanti Feeds has been in a sustained uptrend for months.

There’s also a longer-term story at play. Government focus on improving quality standards, increasing value-added exports, and expanding into new global markets has strengthened the sector’s outlook. Investors aren’t just reacting to current export data—they’re pricing in the possibility of sustained growth over the coming years.

Finally, trading volumes spiked, indicating strong participation. When more buyers enter the market than usual, it reflects bullish sentiment and can push prices up sharply in a short period. (Total traded value (combined for Avanti Feeds + Apex Frozen Foods = 671.8 crores))

Put together, the rally in seafood stocks was not just a reaction to a single data point. It was driven by a combination of strong export growth, resilience in the face of global challenges, sustained international demand, and an already favorable market trend. In essence, the data reinforced a simple but powerful narrative: the earnings outlook for India’s seafood exporters just got better, and the market moved quickly to reflect that.

title: Tata Consumer sees strong traction in growth businesses - The HinduBusinessLine
raw_text:
Sunil D’Souza, MD, CEO, Tata Consumer
																															| Photo Credit:
											Amit Vijay Mohile _12460

Tata Consumer Products is seeing sustained momentum in its growth businesses even as urban discretionary demand remains uneven, with the company sharpening focus on profitability-led expansion and premium categories, Sunil D’Souza, MD & CEO, Tata Consumer, said.

The company recently approved a capital investment of up to ₹160 crore to set up a new 2,000  tonne instant tea manufacturing facility in India, signalling a stronger push into higher-value beverage formats and export opportunities.

Speaking after the company’s Q4FY26 results, D’Souza said growth businesses now contribute nearly a third of the India portfolio, reflecting Tata Consumer’s gradual shift beyond its traditional tea-and-salt identity.

“Tea continues to remain a very strong category for us, but newer categories and growth businesses are becoming increasingly important drivers of the portfolio,” he said.

On the new instant tea facility, D’Souza said the investment is aimed at strengthening the company’s position in value-added tea formats amid rising global demand for ready-to-drink and convenience-led beverage solutions.

The comments come at a time when the company is also recalibrating expansion at Tata Starbucks amid softer urban discretionary spending trends and rising competitive intensity in premium cafés.

D’Souza said discretionary consumption continues to remain uneven across certain urban pockets, impacting traffic growth in premium café formats.

“We are calibrating expansion based on store economics and long-term viability,” he said, adding that the company has rationalised a few underperforming Starbucks stores as part of normal portfolio optimisation rather than chasing aggressive expansion.

He added that categories linked to convenience, health and premiumisation continue to see relatively stronger traction despite broader consumption pressures.

Tata Consumer has been expanding aggressively across packaged foods, ready-to-drink beverages and health-focused products through acquisitions such as Capital Foods and Organic India, while also scaling innovation-led launches across channels including quick commerce

title: Majority stake sale brewing at tea & wellness brand Vahdam India ; top MNC & consumer firms tapped
raw_text:
Direct-to-consumer (D2C) wellness brand Vahdam India which sells green tea, herbal infusions and supplements is in value-unlocking mode and has initiated the process to sell a majority stake in the Noida-headquartered firm, multiple industry sources in the know told Moneycontrol.

“The transaction was launched recently and will facilitate an exit for the VC funds and other investors in Vahdam which has a diversified cap table,” said one of the persons above.

360 One Asset Management, Fireside Ventures and Sixth Sense Ventures are the key external investors in the internet-first firm and the trio hold more than 40 per cent stake , with numerous angel investors including Sachin Tendulkar and Abhishek Bachchan holding nearly 15 per cent stake, as per latest data on Tracxn, a private markets data provider.

According to a second person, “Finding a suitable strategic buyer would be the plan here and hence several top MNC’s and domestic strategics have been tapped for the proposed deal.”

“These are early days and feelers are likely to have been sent to the likes of Nestle, Mars Foods, Orkla, Nepal’s Chaudhary Group , Britannia, ITC, Marico and other industry players,” a third person said.

According to a fourth person, “Axis Capital and Alvarez & Marsal have been engaged as the joint-sell side advisors. The company has been export-oriented in the past but going ahead, there will be increased focus on the Indian market too.”

A fifth person said that non-binding offers for Vahdam India were expected in the month of May.

All the five persons above spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Email queries to the Vahdam founder and CEO Bala Sarda, Fireside Ventures, Sixth Sense Ventures and the MNCs and domestic strategic players were left unanswered at the time of publishing this article. Text messages to Sarda were also left unanswered. Reminders have been sent and this article will be updated as soon as we hear from the parties. An immediate comment couldn’t be elicited from Alvarez & Marsal and Axis Capital. When contacted, 360 One Asset Management declined to comment.

Founder Bala Sarda, a fourth-generation entrepreneur who comes from a family with over 90 years of lineage in the tea industry holds around 20 per cent, as per Tracxn. In 2023, celebrity chef Vikas Khanna was appointed as the brand ambassador for Vahdam’s new range of spices.

Moneycontrol could not independently verify the exact quantum of the stake up for grabs and the names of the selling shareholders.

What’s brewing in the tea and wellness segment?

Vahdam posted revenues of Rs 273 crore as on March 31,2025, a 16 per cent year-on-year increase. It also turned profitable in FY24-25 at Rs 5.2 crores, a 130 per cent year-on-year hike. The firm had a post-money valuation of Rs 825 crore ( $95.2 mn) as on February 24, 2025, as per Tracxn. According to its website, Vahdam also has offices in California, USA and Belfast, UK.

Other brands in the tea and tea blends segment include Darjeeling Tea Boutique, Dorje Tea’s, No 3 Clive Road, Teabox and Karma Kettle.

In January, 2024, in a deal in the same segment, Tata Consumer Products announced that it had signed definitive agreements to acquire up to 100% of Organic India, focused on herbal supplements, tea & infusions and organic packaged foods. The deal was struck for Rs 1,900 crore and valued the company at a little over five times its FY24 sales.

Moneycontrol was the first to report that Tata Consumer had edged ahead of rival suitors like ITC and emerged as the front-runner for Organic India.
